title: Centralize route metadata store and rewrite fanout logic to reduce contention
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Over the last two quarters we've accumulated multiple copies of route metadata (affinity rules, region leases, policy hints) across the smart-router hotpath. This duplication increases GC pressure, causes stale decisions when partial writes occur, and forces broad fanout on policy changes. Several outages (see incident notes) correlate with expensive fanout operations and lock contention while evaluating per-request policy decisions.

Goal: Replace scattered in-memory metadata with a thin, sharded route-metadata store that is the single source of truth for route evaluation. Rewrite the fanout path to a push-based propagation (change-events -> per-shard diff apply) with a compact in-memory index optimized for lookups on decision hotpaths. Reduce lock scope and eliminate the global route lock during evaluation.

Scope & non-goals: This ticket covers the core data structure, sharded in-memory store, fanout rewrite and a compatibility shim for older evaluators. It does NOT include UI changes to the Console or tenant-facing rollout controls (those will be separate). The initial rollout targets region-affinity and policy-hint flows; circuit-breaker and regional quota propagation will be handled in a follow-up.

Success metrics: p50 routing evaluation latency improvement >= 15% on steady-state workloads; p99 improvement >= 10%; CPU usage on routing service reduced by >= 12% during 95th percentile throughput; elimination of global route-lock in hotpath; reduce change-fanout burst CPU spikes by >= 60% during policy updates.

High-level plan: 1) Spike and design doc (done) 2) Implement sharded metadata store with versioned diffs and an in-memory compact index 3) Implement push-based fanout producer and per-shard apply worker 4) Provide compatibility shim for evaluators to read from either old cache or new store with feature flag 5) Incremental rollout with telemetry & kill-switch 6) Remove old caches and locks after 100% stable rollout and two-week burn-in.

Key implementation notes: - Sharding will use (route_id % 64) to avoid hot shards initially; will add adaptive shard rebalancer in follow-up if needed. - Diff propagation uses protobuf v4 delta messages (must align with ENG-51420 protobuf bump). - Per-shard apply is single-writer to avoid fine-grained locks; readers use atomic pointer-swaps to lock-free replace compacted index. - Keep a short-lived write-ahead-log for restart recovery; target < 500ms recovery with warm snapshots.

Risks & mitigations: - Migration complexity: use feature-flagged dual-read mode and per-tenant canaries. - Compatibility regressions: provide compatibility shim and integration test harness that runs both evaluators side-by-side in CI. - Latency regressions on first rollout: start with low-traffic tenants and increase via canary autoscaling.

Rollout strategy: - Stage 1: rollout to internal tenants + 2 low-traffic customers (1 day) - Stage 2: 10% production traffic for 48h with telemetry gates - Stage 3: 50% for 72h - Stage 4: 100% post-green

Dual-read compatibility shim present and exercised in CI
Push-based fanout implemented with per-shard applier and WAL recovery
Perf gates met on internal canaries (p50 >= 15% improvement, CPU <= -12%)
Rollback path and kill-switch tested and documented
Telemetry dashboards show expected reduction in fanout burst CPU and allocation churn
